title: Seven silent days (Job 2:11–13)
hook: Job's friends sit with him seven days without a word, the best thing they do

segments.voice: Yesterday, Job tore his robe and said, the LORD gave and the LORD hath taken away. Your line was naked came I out of my mother's womb. This week ran from Naomi's bitterness, through Ruth's promise and the handfuls in the field, to King David's family line and the land of Uz. It ends in silence.
screen: `NAKED CAME I OUT OF MY MOTHER'S WOMB.`

segments.voice: It gets worse. In chapter two the adversary comes back, and this time Job's own body is struck, with sore boils from the sole of his foot to the top of his head. He sits among the ashes, scraping his skin with a broken piece of pottery. His wife tells him to curse God and die. He answers: "shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?" Far off, three friends hear the news: Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar. They arrange to meet, and they travel to Job together, to mourn with him and comfort him.
screen: `BOILS, ASHES, A BROKEN POT.` → `SHALL WE NOT RECEIVE EVIL?` → `THREE FRIENDS SET OUT.`

segments.voice: From a distance, they don't recognize him. They weep out loud, tear their robes, and throw dust into the air so it falls on their heads. Then the line this day is named for: "So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great." On the ground, in the ashes, at his level. And none of them spoke, because they saw: this grief was bigger than anything they could say. Some readers call this the best thing the friends do in the whole book. Hold on to that, because soon they'll start talking. The rabbis learned something practical here. The Talmud teaches that people who come to comfort a mourner shouldn't speak until the mourner speaks first, and it draws that rule from Job: his friends waited, and Job opened his mouth. Jewish mourning still has a week of sitting, called shiva, when the family stays home and visitors come to them. The custom is to come in, sit down, and let the mourner lead. It's a hard skill. When someone is hurting, the urge to fill the air is strong: an explanation, a story, a bright side. For seven days, the friends resisted it. They brought only themselves.
screen: `THEY DIDN'T RECOGNIZE HIM.` · `THEY SAT DOWN WITH HIM.` · then, large: `NONE SPAKE A WORD UNTO HIM.` · then: `WAIT FOR THE MOURNER TO SPEAK.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone carrying something heavy right now, and picture sitting beside them, on the floor if you like, close enough to touch shoulders. Notice the words that rise up to fix it, and let each one go unsaid; just stay. If you pray, you can hold them before God without words.
Shiva. The seven days Job's friends sat on the ground with him, saying nothing, because they saw how great his grief was. Today's word.
Your line: they said nothing. Sometimes being there is the whole message. Day eight hundred forty, done.

howItsDone: During shiva, the week of mourning, Jewish mourners stay at home and visitors come to comfort them; by tradition visitors wait for the mourner to speak first, a custom the Talmud ties to Job's friends.
